core.title: Draw component events only from the owning feature's declared event sets
core.given: A component belonging to a feature declares consumed or produced events, or dependencies
core.when: the planner authors, edits or reviews those events or dependencies, or changes the feature's declared event sets
core.then: Every declared consumed event must come from the owning feature's declared consumed-event set and fit the component's role, and every declared produced event from the feature's declared produced-event set and fit its capability, so all component events are a subset of, and traceable to, an event the feature declared.
prefer: Need a new event? Add it to the feature's declared event sets first, then reference it.
Pick only the declared events the component's role actually consumes / its capability actually produces; the filter selects, it does not force inclusion of every declared event.
avoid: Inventing inputs/outputs the feature never declared (e.g. producing an event absent from the feature's declared produced-event set).
Events not selected by the role (consume) or capability (produce) filter.
More than 3 consumed or 3 produced events per component.
Dependencies other than same-feature components or external dependencies.
core.why: Limiting component events to the feature's declared event sets keeps each component's interface within its feature's declared contract, so no component invents inputs or outputs the feature never promised.
evidence: For each component, its declared consumed events are a subset of the owning feature's declared consumed-event set and its declared produced events are a subset of the feature's declared produced-event set.

Each consumed event is justified by the component's role and each produced event by its capability (filtered from the respective declared event set); reviewer states the role/capability link per event.
Each component lists at most 3 consumed and at most 3 produced events.
Compliant example: a component consumes an event that the owning feature's declared consumed-event set includes.
Violation example: a component produces an event that the owning feature's declared produced-event set does not contain.
Component dependencies come from other components in the same feature plus external dependencies.
verification: Subset check: all consumed/produced events declared on a component must be traceable to the owning feature's declared event sets; the checker resolves the owning feature from the plan artifact and compares the component's event lists against the feature's sets. The concrete field names for the feature's sets and the component's event lists come from the profile's plan-artifact syntax.

Consumed events are sourced from the feature's declared consumed-event set filtered by the component's role and produced events from the declared produced-event set filtered by its capability; at most 3 consumed and 3 produced events per component.
Dependency-source check: each component dependency must resolve to a component of the same feature or to an external dependency; the reference shapes for both come from the profile.

The subset check is per declared event: if the owning feature's declared event set for a direction is absent or empty, any declared event in that direction is untraceable and is a finding; a component with no declared events in that direction produces no event-subset finding, but its dependencies are still checked against the dependency-source rule. No minimum number of events is required.

No automated implementation exists in the reference realization; the check is reviewer/LLM-judged until a diff-level observer over component event/dependency lists and a set-comparison checker are built. The role/capability fit of an event is a semantic judgement.
Scope: the check targets plan artifacts (which concrete artifact kinds count as plan artifacts comes from the profile); code-level changes that do not touch planning artifacts do not fire.

values: plan artifact carrying a component's consume/produce/dependency lists
plan artifact carrying a feature's declared event sets
component consume/produce list added or edited
feature declared event set added, edited or removed
declared component event not in the owning feature's declared event set
more than 3 consumed or more than 3 produced events
dependency neither same-feature component nor external
declared event not relevant to component role (consume) or capability (produce)

fires: Planner declares a component that produces an event absent from the owning feature's declared produced-event set.
Planner adds a consumed event to a component that the feature's declared consumed-event set does not list.
Planner changes a feature's declared event sets so an existing component's declared events are no longer a subset.
Planner gives a component a consumed event unrelated to its role, or a produced event unrelated to its capability.
Planner lists a fourth consumed or a fourth produced event on one component.
Planner adds a component dependency on a component of another feature that is not an external dependency.
doesNotFire: A component that declares no consumed or produced events AND whose dependencies are all same-feature components or external dependencies. (Empty event lists alone only satisfy the event-subset part; dependency sourcing must still be checked.)
Authoring a feature's declared event sets before any component of that feature declares events or dependencies.
Code-level changes that do not touch planning artifacts.

profileRequirements.meaning: The plan-artifact syntax this rule binds to: the fields where a feature declares its consumed and produced event sets, and the fields where a component declares its consumed and produced events. The core's phrases 'the owning feature's declared consumed-/produced-event set' and 'the component's declared events' (and the activation task term 'declared event sets') resolve to these fields.
profileRequirements.bunValue: Feature's event sets: feature.ioSeeds.consume and feature.ioSeeds.produce. Component's event lists: consumes and produces.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kinds that carry component consume/produce/dependency lists and a feature's declared event sets, so the rule's activation facts and the checker can target them; the core states these kinds only at role level.
Reference shape of a component, used to recognise a same-feature component dependency and to resolve the owning feature of a component.
The reference shape, inside a plan artifact's component dependency list, that counts as an external dependency (as opposed to a component of another feature).

neutralityNotes: The rule's planning vocabulary (feature, component, consume/produce, dependencies, planner) belongs to the ATDD planning model, not to any runtime stack, so it stays in the core. The concrete plan-schema field names are NOT kept in the core: ioSeeds, feature.ioSeeds.consume and feature.ioSeeds.produce (and the component's consumes/produces lists) are the Bun plan syntax, supplied as idiom.plan_syntax#component_events; the core refers only to 'the owning feature's declared consumed-/produced-event set' and 'the component's declared events' (title, when, then, prefer, avoid[0], evidence, verification and activation all rephrased accordingly), so a stack with the same planning roles does not have to adopt these field names. The 3-event cap is a methodology constant and stays in the core. What else varies per stack - which concrete artifact kinds are plan artifacts and how component / external-dependency references are shaped - is taken from the profile (roles.plan_artifact.kinds, urn.component, urn.grammar#external_dependency). Concrete example events, reference ids and the Bun kind names are not repeated in the core; bun.json remains the worked reference example. 'implementation.type: none' is the Bun realization's status and is bunOnly; the core states generically that the check is reviewer/LLM-judged until a diff-level observer and set-comparison checker exist. No new vocabulary key was needed.
